title: Breaking: The Snow That Stayed (Part 2)
description: The snow that refused to melt has crept across the parking lot and is now feeling out the lobby. Rhonda still calls it textbook, Sal is so far underwater on his snow leases he can see the bottom, and Winston discovers that owning the only snow in the county means owning everything it does next. Mildred's Kevin, meanwhile, has had family over.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Welcome back to Snazzie FM. When we left you, the town's first snow had stopped being weather and started being a tenant. <p:0.3> It is now in our parking lot. As of this morning, it is sniffing the lobby.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It came inside, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We have not confirmed it came inside, Barry. We're calling it a guest near the door. Rhonda, you've been on the snow all night. What is it doing?

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: So, good news. It's textbook. <p:0.3> Textbook for a snow that has chosen indoor living. Seventy-one degrees in the lobby, Ronnie, and it is, if anything, settling in by the vending machine.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Seventy-one is a pool temperature, Rhonda. That is not a snow number.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: It SHOULD be a pool, Barry. <p:0.3> The textbook is furious about this. The snow has read the textbook and disagreed.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Ronnie, it's Sal. <p:0.3> So my thousand bags? <p:0.3> I leased the ground they sat on too. From three guys. Who all say they own the ground.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Sal, how far underwater are you on this snow.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Underwater? Ronnie, I can see the bottom. <p:0.3> I owe more on snow than the snow weighs. But here's the play. It's spreading, right? So technically my inventory is GROWING.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's not yours, Sal. It's just moving.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: It is moving onto MY deed, Barry. <p:0.3> Ronnie gave me the deed last hour. I predicted this snow, I now legally OWN this snow, and I want it on record that I'm thrilled.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Congratulations, Winston. <p:0.3> Although. A small ownership note. The lobby snow is also yours now. So is the carpet it's eating.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: It's eating the WHAT?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Hi, dear. Quick thing about Kevin. <p:0.3> He had family over. There are four of them on my porch now. The new ones are shy.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Mildred, the snow reproduced?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: I wouldn't say reproduced, dear. I'd say it's a household now. The little one's called Denise.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Okay, update. <p:0.3> The lobby snow and the porch snow are headed for each other. Textbook says snow doesn't have plans. <p:0.3> This snow has an itinerary.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Folks, based on snow with a household and an itinerary, I'm upgrading us to a Tier Three Resident Condition. <p:0.3> Do not name your snow. <p:0.3> If you have already named it, do not introduce it to other snow.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Tier Three! <p:0.3> Okay, given Tier Three, I'm relisting. It's a family-owned snow now. That's a premium product, Ronnie. Eighty a bag.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You owe money on snow that won't melt and you raised the price AGAIN, Sal?

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: It's RARER and it has a kid now, Barry! Same snow, bigger family, scarier paperwork!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: He can't sell my snow's CHILDREN, Ronnie! <p:0.3> The deed says the snow is mine, which means the porch snow is mine, which means Denise is MY snow!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Denise stays with me, dear.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: Tiny correction, everyone. <p:0.3> The two snows just met in the hallway. They are not fighting. <p:0.3> They are mingling.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Snow does not mingle, Rhonda!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I want OUT of the deed!

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: I'll buy the deed! Ninety a bag, I'll pay in bags!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Denise is not for sale!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Take the deed back, Ronnie!

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: It's textbook mingling!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Everybody hold. <p:0.3> Rhonda. Give me the number.

lines.speaker: rhonda
lines.text: So, Ronnie. <p:0.4> The two snows are now one snow. <p:0.3> It is bigger than both put together. And it has stopped moving an inch a night. <p:0.4> It's doing a foot.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A foot. <p:0.4> Folks, it's no longer a resident. <p:0.3> It's a neighborhood.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Does anybody want a neighborhood? <p:0.3> Lightly used. <p:0.4> ...Slightly mingling?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Nobody's buying a neighborhood made of snow, Sal.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well, there it is, folks. The town's first snow now has a household, a foot of ambition, and, per the deed, a single legal owner. <p:0.3> Winston. <p:0.4> It's at your front door.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: My door? <p:0.3> Ronnie, which way is the foot headed.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Inland, Winston. <p:0.3> Toward the reservoir.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Kevin says he's bringing everyone, dear.
